title: function-calling-parse-incident-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for investigating repeated failures parsing function/tool-calling structured outputs from hosted API. Mostly breadcrumbs (commands tried, snippet of errors, hypotheses).

Background:
- Internal endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (hosted) using function-calling JSON schema mode.
- Regression started 2026-02-18 after model/handler rollout (PR #482). See ENG-1234 for incident ticket.
- Symptoms: ~5% of requests return a payload that fails JSON schema validation (missing required fields or wrong types). Not always reproducible locally.

Repro steps I used (local curl / python):
1) Simple curl to mimic client:
   curl -s -X POST 
     -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" 
     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
     -d '{"model":"rw-v1","input":"Summarize: ...","function_call":{"name":"create_summary","arguments_schema":{}}}' 
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq '.'
   -> sometimes prints partial JSON then error from jq: \"parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 234\"

2) Python client snippet (requests) used to reproduce: 
   resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, stream=True)
   for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
       sys.stdout.write(chunk.decode('utf-8'))
   -> observed model text interleaved with JSON blob (possible streaming boundary issue)

Observed model responses (examples):
- Example A (valid):
  {"name":"create_summary", "arguments": {"summary":"Short...","confidence":0.92}}

- Example B (invalid / common failure):
  {"name":"create_summary", "arguments": {"summary":"Text truncated..."}
  <-- missing closing brace, trailing text: \"generated by tool: id=23\"

- Example C (schema mismatch):
  {"name":"create_summary","arguments":{"summary":12345}}  # summary should be string

What I tried so far (notes):
- jsonschema.validate(...) against schema on server: catches the failures but need to find root cause upstream.
- Increased max_tokens/response window to reduce truncation: no clear impact. Hypothesis: streaming boundary chunking might split braces.
- Forced non-streaming mode (buffer complete response server-side before emitting) -> rare failures still occur. Means not only streaming.
- Added content-length check & reassembly on client: mitigates some cases but not all.
- Regex attempt: tried to extract the first top-level JSON object with this pattern: (?s)\{.*?\}\s*$ and also greedy variants. Works for 60-70% but breaks when model emits trailing explanatory text with extra braces.
- Attempted lenient JSON parser (demjson, python's simplejson with allow_nan False) — helps for numeric issues, not for structural truncation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model occasionally emits extra explanatory text after JSON payload (e.g., \"generated by tool: ...\") and our client/server pipeline concatenates that with the JSON in a way that causes schema failures.
2) The runner post-processing (the code that transforms model text -> function call object) has a bug when stripping out assistant/system annotations (see recent change in PR #482). Edge case: stray backslashes or escaped quotes cause a premature end-of-json detection.
3) Quantization / tokenization change causes the model to generate unescaped control chars occasionally, leading to JSON.parse errors on the client.
4) Rate-limiting/backpressure causing truncated responses (less likely because non-streaming still fails sometimes).

Immediate next steps to pin down root cause (who/what to ping):
- Reproduce with pinned model weights + disabled PR #482 changes (Ethan to run A/B job).
- Add verbose logging in runner: raw_model_text -> post_processed_text -> json_attempts (store each attempt and parse error). Add sampling for failed requests (keep first 200 chars + last 200 chars).
- Add a small heuristic sanitizer for now: if trailing text after top-level JSON contains only printable words (like 'generated by tool'), drop it and parse. Keep as temporary mitigation.
- Run a corpus-level scan of last 24h failures (via observability: logs/trace ids) and save 50 examples for analysis. Jira: ENG-1234 assigned to Priya.

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Slack thread: #dev-tools (ts: 2026-02-19 11:14) — Priya reported initial spike.
- Runner commit that might be suspect: repo@c4f2e3d (PR #482).
- Confluence spec for function-call schema: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Function+Call+Spec
- Quick grep for 'closing brace' in runner: found a strip() call in postprocess.py lines ~142-148 — suspicious (might drop last brace if whitespace trimming is naive).

Quick temporary fix patch idea (to deploy to staging):
- In runner postprocess: when extracting JSON, use a robust bracket-matching approach instead of first/last index of '{' and '}'. Pseudocode:
    find first '{' index i
    walk forward with depth counter: depth +=1 on '{', depth -=1 on '}'
    when depth == 0, take substring [i..j] as candidate JSON. Attempt json.loads. If fails, store raw for inspection.

Questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Is there any post-processing that intentionally appends diagnostics to the assistant output? (search for 'generated by tool' in codebase).
- Add a small regression test in unit tests: model stub that returns JSON+trailing text, ensure parser extracts JSON correctly.
- Decide whether to treat trailing text as fatal or lenient (configurable switch).

Scratchpad outputs (raw captured snippets):
- SNIPPET #12 (2026-02-21T09:17Z): \"{\"name\":\"create_summary\", \"arguments\": {\"summary\": \"...\"}\"generated by tool: id=23\"\n- SNIPPET #19 (2026-02-22T14:04Z): \"{\"name\":\"create_summary\", \"arguments\": {\"summary\": 456}}\n- SNIPPET #24 (2026-02-23T01:02Z): partial JSON then EOF (socket close)

If anyone picks this up: start by reproducing locally with the runner pinned at c4f2e3d and model pinned at rw-v1. I left a small test script in my home dir: ~/scripts/repro_function_parse.py (not checked in).

-- Jordan
